Performers
United States Marine Band (wind ensemble with contrabassoon and double bass), Timothy Foley (conductor) Documented

The booklet marks the players participating in the Rossini: flute, two oboes, two B-flat clarinets, two bassoons, contrabassoon, two horns and string bass. No trumpet or cello performance is attributed to this transcription.

[3] [2] [1]
Work version
Wind-ensemble transcription attributed to Wenzel Sedlak, adapted for the Marine Band’s Grand Scenes recording Documented

The booklet explicitly says the attribution to Sedlak has not been conclusively proved. The overture comes from a fifteen-movement suite preserved at the Augustinian monastery in Brno. For this recording, the flute part was modified using Rossini’s orchestral part, two added trumpet parts were removed, and contrabassoon and string bass reinforced the bass. This is a small wind ensemble with double bass, not Rossini’s original full orchestral scoring.

Recorded
2000-06-05/2000-06-09 Documented

The album was recorded during this five-day period. The day and take used for the overture are not separately identified.

Transfer
Original editing and mastering: Bob Katz, Digital Domain. Wikimedia Commons upload: TonyTheTiger. Documented

The booklet separately credits producers Denis R. Burian and Michael J. Colburn, and recording engineers Karl J. Jackson and Kevan D. Lewis. These original production credits are distinct from the later Commons upload and MP3 conversion.

[3] [1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The original capture medium and dates of mastering and Ogg conversion are not documented. Commons records the current Ogg upload on 14 April 2011; that is not a recording-session date.

[3] [1]
Processing
Ogg Vorbis file on Wikimedia Commons, with a Commons-hosted MP3 transcode. Documented

The file page credits the Marine Band’s web audio as its source. The exact intervening conversion settings, original capture chain, equalisation and any noise processing are not established.

[1]
Composition rights
The historical composition and the arrangement used on this album are identified as public domain. Documented

Rossini died in 1868. The official booklet states that its selections are public domain unless otherwise noted; it places no copyright exception on this overture. The qualified Sedlak attribution is retained rather than treating uncertain authorship as proof of rights.

[3] [1] [6]
Recording rights
US public domain — official United States Marine Band recording, tagged PD-USGov-⁠Military-⁠Marines by Wikimedia Commons. Documented

The official album and booklet corroborate the federal performance and production. Section 105 excludes qualifying US Government works from US copyright protection; this is not a Creative Commons licence or an assertion that every government work is public domain in every jurisdiction.
